clue.text: Unconventional piano discovered by old man during black mass

indicators.note: during means the old-man letters sit within the black-and-mass pair

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
M is the physics symbol for mass
he is the pronoun for a man

indicators.note: discovered means uncovered, so the word piano loses its outer letters

explanation.surface: A rule-breaking pianist is spotted by an old man in the middle of a satanic black mass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' puts OHE inside B and M, giving BOHEM; 'discovered' strips the cover letters from piano to leave IAN, and 'by' simply places it alongside.
explanation.definitionFit: A bohemian lives an unconventional, artistic life outside social norms, so the adjective is a synonym.

clue.text: Man is hot, occupying branch office 20

indicators.note: occupying means the is-hot letters take up space inside the branch-office-and-pawn string

parts.note: BO is the abbreviation for branch office
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
20 down is PAWN, written P in chess notation

explanation.surface: Someone is having a hot time at a branch office.
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle is themed on chess, so 'Man' means a chess piece and the cross-reference 20 (PAWN) gives its notation letter P.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess the pieces are called men, and the bishop is one of them.

clue.text: 24A vacated hostile country

indicators.note: vacated means emptied of contents, so only the outside letters of hostile remain

parts.note: Cuba is a Caribbean country

explanation.surface: A queen abandoned a hostile country.
explanation.walkthrough: 24A is QUEEN; Hecuba was queen of Troy in Greek legend.
explanation.definitionFit: Hecuba, wife of King Priam, was the legendary queen of Troy, so she is an example of a queen.

clue.text: Operatic heroine taking in American city

indicators.note: taking in means the heroine's name holds the American letter inside it

parts.note: Mimi is the heroine of Puccini's La Boheme

explanation.surface: An opera heroine welcomes an American to the city.
explanation.walkthrough: Mimi of La Boheme also links back to 1 across, BOHEMIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Miami is a large city in Florida, an example of the general word city.

clue.text: Norm greeting artist on the way up, say

parts.note: ave is the Latin greeting 'hail'
RA is a Royal Academician, a painter

indicators.note: on the way up in a down clue means the letters for 'say' are read upwards, in reverse

parts.note: eg, for example, is what 'say' means

explanation.surface: Norm says hello to a painter whose career is rising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Norm' looks like a man's name, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The average is the norm, the usual or typical standard.

clue.text: Man's 21A near Thailand

parts.note: 21 across is KING, written K in chess notation
nigh is an old word for near
T is the international vehicle code for Thailand

explanation.surface: A man's king lives close to Thailand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is a chess piece throughout the puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: The knight is one of the chess men, the piece that moves in an L shape.

clue.text: DEA agent, having dumped cocaine, almost shares story

indicators.note: having dumped means the drug letter is thrown out of the agent

parts.note: a narc is an American narcotics agent, as in the Drug Enforcement Administration
C is slang shorthand for cocaine

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the shares word is dropped

parts.note: rations are allotted shares

explanation.surface: A drug agent who got rid of seized cocaine is nearly sharing it out.
explanation.walkthrough: A narc (NARC) losing C gives NAR; RATIONS cut short gives RATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Narration is the telling of a story, an account of events.

clue.text: Tumblers emptied, groggy men assess tequilas

indicators.note: emptied means each word loses its contents, leaving only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Glasses are drained as drunk men size up their tequila shots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tumblers' suggests drinking glasses beside the tequila, but means acrobats.
explanation.definitionFit: Tumblers are acrobats performing somersaults and flips, as gymnasts do.

clue.text: Demolish pâté and the last of the spread

indicators.note: demolish means knock to pieces, so the letters are rearranged
last of means only the final letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: Wolf down the pâté and finish off the spread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Demolish' reads as eating heartily; here it shuffles PATE AND into TAPENAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Tapenade is a Provençal paste of olives, capers and anchovies spread on bread.

clue.text: Philosopher's very good bangers

parts.note: so! can be an exclamation of approval, like 'very good'
bangers and crates are both slang for old, rattly cars

explanation.surface: A thinker's cars are really excellent old wrecks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bangers' is British slang for decrepit old cars, not sausages.
explanation.definitionFit: Socrates was the Athenian thinker who taught Plato, the archetypal Greek philosopher.

clue.text: Party adopting unusual petition

indicators.note: adopting means the party takes the unusual word into itself

parts.note: DUP is the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland
rum means odd or unusual

explanation.surface: A political party takes up an unusual petition.
explanation.definitionFit: To drum up is to solicit or canvass for support or business, as a petition seeks backing.

clue.text: Man's run over — fine

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
O is the cricket abbreviation for over
OK means fine

explanation.surface: A cricketer's run is finished, and all is well.
explanation.definitionFit: The rook, or castle, is one of the chess men.

clue.text: Ordinary 1D got bail-out that must be used in performance

definitions.text: that must be used in performance

parts.note: O is an abbreviation for ordinary, as in O level
1 down is BISHOP, written B in chess notation

indicators.note: out means the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: An ordinary bishop got a bail-out.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'out' of 'bail-out' signals rearranging GOT BAIL into BLIGATO.
explanation.definitionFit: An obbligato is a musical part the composer marks as indispensable, so it must be played in performance.

clue.text: Australian silverback at home once more

parts.note: Ag, the chemical symbol for silver, turned back gives GA
in means at home

explanation.surface: An Australian gorilla is at home again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'silverback' looks like a gorilla but splits into silver (AG, its chemical symbol) and 'back', which turns it to GA.
explanation.definitionFit: Again and once more are synonyms meaning a further time.

clue.text: See 26
Movement seen in Scotland — Antinomianism?

indicators.note: seen in means the answer is visible inside the following words

explanation.surface: A religious movement found in Scotland, perhaps antinomian in belief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Movement' suggests a religious or political cause; it is a piece of music.
explanation.definitionFit: Andantino is a tempo marking, and a symphony's movement may be named after its tempo.

clue.text: 21A, 5, 1: Times editor used needles

parts.note: 21 across is KING, K in chess notation
5 across is KNIGHT, N in chess notation
1 is I in Roman numerals
T is short for time, so times, the plural, doubles it to TT

explanation.surface: A list of chess pieces and a Times editor who used needles.
explanation.walkthrough: In chess notation a knight is N, since K is taken by the king.
explanation.definitionFit: To have knitted is to have worked yarn with needles.

clue.text: Well-spoken lot 24A upset

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: 24 across is QUEEN

explanation.surface: A well-spoken crowd upset the queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Eloquent describes fluent, persuasive speech, so it means well-spoken.

clue.text: Offer at a lower price than tenderloin?

definitions.text: Offer at a lower price than
definitions.meaning: to sell more cheaply than a rival
the beef ... is the tenderloin, a cut taken from beneath the sirloin; the question mark marks it as an example

explanation.surface: Selling the tenderloin more cheaply than the shop next door.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: undercutting is pricing below a rival, and the undercut is the tenderloin of beef.

clue.text: Queued for starter of devils on horseback next to range

parts.note: a line can be a range, as in a product line

indicators.note: starter of means the first letter of devils

parts.note: a jockey who is up is mounted on horseback

explanation.surface: Waiting for a devils-on-horseback starter, the prunes-in-bacon appetiser.
explanation.walkthrough: Devils on horseback are a British starter of bacon-wrapped prunes; here 'starter' just means first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To be lined up is to stand in a line, which is what queuing is.

clue.text: Man and wife look for gold boxes

indicators.note: boxes means encloses, so the panning letters surround the wife letter

parts.note: to pan is to sift river gravel for gold

explanation.surface: A husband and wife go prospecting for gold.
explanation.definitionFit: The pawn is the humblest of the chess men.

clue.text: Man from London area after leaving pub

indicators.note: after leaving means the pub word departs from the area name

parts.note: Barking is a district of east London
a bar is a pub

explanation.surface: A man from east London heads home after leaving the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: BARKING is a district of east London.
explanation.definitionFit: The king is the central piece among the chess men.

clue.text: 5A remains on edge, climbing disputed region

parts.note: 5 across is KNIGHT, abbreviated K in titles such as KBE
ash is what remains after burning

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means the edge word is read upwards

parts.note: a rim is an edge

explanation.surface: A knight's remains lie on an edge, climbing into contested land.
explanation.walkthrough: Here K stands for knight as in honours like KBE, not chess notation.
explanation.definitionFit: Kashmir is a Himalayan territory whose sovereignty India, Pakistan and China contest.

clue.text: Baleful sickness upset no-good individual

parts.note: mal is a sickness, as in mal de mer

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means these letters are turned upside down, read in reverse

parts.note: NG is short for no good
I, one, is an individual

explanation.surface: An evil illness unsettles a worthless person.
explanation.definitionFit: Malign and baleful both mean evil in nature or effect, harmful.

clue.text: Mean runner married Penny, heartlessly

parts.note: a ski is a runner on snow

indicators.note: heartlessly means the middle letters are removed, leaving the ends

explanation.surface: A tight-fisted runner wed Penny without any feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runner' suggests an athlete but is a ski, which runs over snow.
explanation.definitionFit: Skimpy and mean both describe something meagre or stingy in amount.

clue.text: Tom's mate, man and woman leading band

definitions.meaning: a tom is a male cat, and its mate is a female cat
a chess man, the most powerful piece
the female monarch heads the realm, and the name is also that of the rock band of Freddie Mercury

explanation.surface: A cat's partner, plus a man and woman fronting a group.
explanation.definitionFit: A female cat, a chess piece, a female monarch and a rock band share this one name.

clue.text: One half of comedy duo prior to expert joke

parts.note: Ernie Wise was half of the British double act Morecambe and Wise
crack means expert, as in a crack shot

explanation.surface: A comedian's partner is an expert at jokes.
explanation.walkthrough: Morecambe and Wise were a much-loved British TV comedy double act.
explanation.definitionFit: A wisecrack is a smart, witty remark, a kind of quip.

clue.text: Picked up 1A friend, perhaps — defeat for 21A?

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: 1 across is BOHEMIAN, and a Bohemian is a Czech
a mate is a friend, perhaps

explanation.surface: Collecting a Bohemian pal, maybe: the downfall of the king.
explanation.walkthrough: Bohemia is the western region of the Czech Republic.
explanation.definitionFit: Checkmate is the defeat of a chess king, when it is attacked with no escape.

clue.text: Cryptic clue, 1D: Alexandrian summer?

indicators.note: cryptic means puzzling and obscure, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: the characters 1D are read as letters, I and D

explanation.surface: A puzzle clue pointing to 1 down, the cryptic setter's playground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'summer' means one who sums, a mathematician, not the season; '1D' is read as the letters ID.
explanation.definitionFit: Euclid, geometer of Alexandria, was a mathematician, jokingly one who does sums.

clue.text: One parent holding fairy's power to command

parts.note: I is one in Roman numerals

indicators.note: holding means the parent contains the fairy

parts.note: mum is a parent
a peri is a fairy of Persian legend; the 's links the pieces

explanation.surface: A single parent clutches a fairy's magical power.
explanation.definitionFit: Imperium is the Latin for supreme authority, the right to command.

clue.text: Touch up Ringo's drumming

definitions.meaning: to tap or beat on something repeatedly, a run of light touches
a rhythmic beating on a drum, as by the Beatles drummer Ringo Starr

explanation.surface: Smartening up the beat of a Beatle.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to rap or drum steadily; as a noun it is a rhythmic drumbeat.

clue.text: Intermittently, relative left youth-leader outside disreputable house

indicators.note: outside means these letters go around the house letters

parts.note: bro is short for brother, a relative

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of youth

parts.note: ken is old slang for a house, especially a thieves' den

explanation.surface: A relative left the youth leader outside a house of ill repute.
explanation.walkthrough: KEN is an old cant word for a den of thieves.
explanation.definitionFit: Brokenly means in fits and starts, with interruptions, so it means intermittently.
